guidance: Space planning only. The Sphere figures are humanitarian minimums for covered living space, not legal occupancy limits; egress, fire separation, ventilation, structural capacity, accessibility and local building rules are not assessed, and cold climates or longer stays need more space.
method: Covered living space is the floor area left after circulation, cooking, bathing, sanitation and storage are taken out, so the page first applies the non-living share: living area = floor area x (1 - share / 100). The headcount times the chosen space per person gives the living area needed, and the living area available divided by that need gives the share of the target met. Living area per person is the available living area divided by the headcount. The people the floor shelters is the whole-number floor of the available living area divided by the space per person, so capacity times the target never exceeds the living area and one more person always would. The gross floor needed for the headcount is the living area needed divided by (1 - share / 100), and its square root and the square root of the available floor give square footprints for comparison. A fixed list applies the same floor to 2, 3, 3.5, 4.5 and 5.5 square metres per person so capacity can be compared across space standards. The 3.5 m2 figure is the Sphere minimum covered living area per person in hot climates, with 4.5 m2 used in cold climates; the page lets any target from 1 to 20 m2 be entered. Inputs allow 1 to 10000 people, 1 to 1000000 square metres of floor, 1 to 20 square metres per person and a non-living share of 0 to 80 percent, with at most two decimals on areas and one on the share. Blank, non-numeric and out-of-range values are refused with an actionable message. The calculation runs entirely in the browser with no storage, uploads or network access.
